const.description: Returns the blocks a mounted image holds although its filesystem freed them, WHILE the image stays mounted and in use. macOS (measured, see the ticket note): a DiskImages2 image attached with `diskutil image attach` forwards APFS trim to the backing file as hole punching, but APFS flushes the trim of its container only when a volume of that container unmounts. A sibling APFS volume `semio-trim` in the same container, created, mounted and unmounted again and deleted at the end of the cycle (a second volume would make `diskutil image attach --mountPoint` fail for the image on its next attach: it works only for an image with a single mountable entity), therefore returns every freed block in about two seconds without touching the busy main volume (open files, working directories and concurrent writers are unaffected; fsck_apfs is clean). The legacy `hdiutil attach` stack never unmaps. `hdiutil compact` of a sparse bundle or sparse image refuses while attached. Linux: the backing is a sparse loop file; `fstrim` on the mounted filesystem punches holes (FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE). Windows has no in-place return: a dynamic VHDX compacts only while dismounted or mounted read-only, so the platform is `offline-only` and relies on the drain window of the exclusive reclaim cycle.

ineffective.en: Image {image} did not give back a 256 MiB test file after the in-place kick ({returned} of {written} returned). macOS only unmaps containers up to 32 GiB (measured: 34.36 GB works, 35.43 GB never does, in place or by detach and attach), so this image cannot return freed blocks. Split it into images of at most 32 GiB or accept its high-water size.
ineffective.de: Das Image {image} gab nach dem direkten Anstoß eine 256-MiB-Testdatei nicht zurück ({returned} von {written} zurückgegeben). macOS gibt nur bei Containern bis 32 GiB Blöcke frei (gemessen: 34,36 GB funktionieren, 35,43 GB nie, weder direkt noch durch Lösen und Anhängen), dieses Image kann freie Blöcke also nicht zurückgeben. Teile es in Images von höchstens 32 GiB oder akzeptiere seine Höchstgröße.

outputs.description: Successive stdout values of a command keyed by `<program name> <first argument>`; the last value repeats; an absent key prints nothing.

expected.description: The commands run in order, each `<program name> <arguments joined by one space>`, `<scratch>` standing for the private scratch mount point.
